text:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High severity - GPU OOM cascade on serving-prod-eu. Metric: container_restart_rate spike (service=runtime-prefill). Multiple containers failing during prefill of large-context requests. First alert at 1718012345.

sam: I'm oncall, looking now. Which nodes are the hot ones?

anya: seeing a restart loop on node gpu-eu-07 and gpu-eu-09. Prefill pods hit OOM while allocating KV cache for long prompts (~>200k tokens workload).

marta: confirmed CUDA OOM in runtime logs. snippet: 
```
2026-03-10T12:05:12Z runtime ERROR cuda: out of memory when allocating tensor(6144, 4096)
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.2 GiB (GPU 0; 31.75 GiB total capacity)
Container exit: code 137 -> kKilled
kubectl describe pod serving-prefill-xyz shows repeated backoff restarts
```

devon: nodes are still healthy at infra level, but GPU memory use jumps to 100% during prefill. Looks like a single tenant is sending huge context windows that bypassed our request size caps.

karen: CS says one customer reported degraded responses ~12:03 UTC. They sent a batched import with very long prompts.

sam: immediate mitigation steps: 1) add a temporary request cap to enforce max prompt tokens = 65k for hosted API 2) route traffic for heavy customers to coldmodels (lower mem) 3) cordon gpu-eu-09 and drain if restarts continue. Who can do routing?

anya: I can deploy a runtime config patch to disable KV prefetch for requests > 32k tokens (hotfix) — small change to server config. Will push canary to one node first.

devon: I'll cordon gpu-eu-09 and spin up two extra nodes in the pool (scale-up) to absorb non-prefill traffic. Also putting taint:dedicated=prefill:NoSchedule to isolate prefill pods.

marta: while hotfix deploys, we should evict in-flight long-context jobs to prevent further OOMs. I can run a job that patches deployments with TTL eviction for pods matching label prefill=true.

sam: assignable: anya -> runtime hotfix, devon -> node cordon + scale, marta -> eviction script, karen/CS -> notify affected customer with ETA. I'll stay on until stabilised.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: runtime-config v2.14.3-hotfix -> canary on gpu-eu-07 (user=anya). CI checks passed.

anya: canary applied to gpu-eu-07, monitoring memory. Initial observations: KV prefetch disabled for >32k requests reduces peak allocation by ~40%.

marta: starting eviction run: `kubectl get pods -l prefill=true -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl delete --grace-period=30` (targeting the largest pods first).

devon: cordoned gpu-eu-09 and scaled nodepool +2 (node IDs queued). Also added autoscaler temporary target to prefer additional nodes in eu region.

sam: memory pressure dropping on gpu-eu-07 after canary, restarts stopped there. gpu-eu-09 still has one restart loop, marta's eviction in progress.

karen: CS update to customer: "We're mitigating a memory issue affecting large-context requests; we've throttled oversized requests and applied a temporary server-side change. We'll share ETA in 30m." They asked for request logs — providing anonymized samples.

marta: eviction finished, containers on gpu-eu-09 restarted cleanly after restart backoff, no further OOM seen for 12 minutes.

anya: rolling hotfix to remaining nodes now (gpu-eu-01..12). Rolling restart scheduled, 30s rolling window.

sam: creating incident ticket (INC-2026-342) for postmortem + action items: 1) enforce hard request token limits in edge layer 2) add per-tenant long-context caps and circuit breaker 3) improve prefill memory accounting in runtime 4) add better telemetry for KV allocations by request 5) customer outreach template.

devon: follow-up infra work: add node-level guard to limit single-pod GPU allocation to 90% memory, and revisit scheduler scoring to avoid packing large prefill pods on same node.

karen: CS will send an updated note in 20m including temporary mitigations and next steps.

sam: current status: runtime memory pressure normalised, no new OOM alerts in last 15m. Keeping channel open for 60m of observation, then we'll de-escalate. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
